rationale: The candidate reads as a compact, centrally tightened multi-faceted mass with a polygonal top and little sectional consequence. In all four views it is coherent enough to hold together, so it is not a pure fragmentation failure, but it is also not a convincing neighborhood-living massing diagram. The dominant gesture is weak: the shape behaves more like a clipped stump or faceted token than a clear active street building. The verified access edge is not answered by a legible public void, court, seam, or entry notch; the blue frontage reads adjacent rather than absorbed into the massing logic. The thin green parcel is contained, but the proposal mainly sits inside the bounding figure rather than organizing itself in response to it. There is almost no meaningful courtyard or undercut, and the upper silhouette is neither especially productive nor clearly programmatic. The references suggest two useful principles: one, a singular mass can be stepped or tapered if the section is intentional; two, neighborhood living benefits from a strong public threshold and/or usable void. This candidate presently lacks both, so program fit fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is much smaller and more stump-like; it lacks the tower/slab hierarchy and vertical pull of the reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered massing can create a clear dominant figure when the section reads as a deliberate capacity-bearing profile.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a tall tower; only the idea of singularity transfers, not the typology or vertical proportion.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong singular mass can be legible even with a tapered or slumped silhouette if the section is coherent.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a low retail object with a clear storefront threshold; the candidate is more centralized and does not resolve frontage as clearly.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple bar with a legible public edge/canopy can support neighborhood commercial ground activation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual by intent; the candidate does not yet achieve the open, inhabited section or long horizontal urbanism of this precedent.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced mass and a usable void can organize neighborhood living around public ground and section.

warnings: Access response is semantically opposite/indifferent rather than active.
No convincing public court, notch, terrace, or ground undercut is visible.
Mass reads as a compact object rather than a neighborhood street building.
Stepping/faceting is present but not meaningfully tied to program or section.
